clue.text: Confidence in start of story, happy tale we hear?

indicators.note: the start of the word story is its opening letter

parts.note: said aloud 'happy tale' is 'happy tail', and a happy dog's tail is one that wags, a wagger

explanation.surface: Someone is confident when beginning a story and telling a cheerful tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' swaps 'tale' for its soundalike 'tail'; a contented dog's tail wags, making it a wagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Swagger is a bold, self-assured manner, an outward show of confidence.

clue.text: Bags of gentlemen actors in play

indicators.note: in a play the actors move around, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: The luggage of gentlemen actors appearing in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrotum is the pouch of skin holding the testes, so males carry these anatomical sacs.

clue.text: See 25
Going, possibly, to leave food, toast lacking a spread

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: spread out, the remaining letters are laid out afresh
the letter a is missing from the breakfast words

explanation.surface: Instructions to abandon food and toast that has nothing spread on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking a' takes A from TOAST; 'spread' rearranges FOOD TOST. Going is horse-racing jargon for the state of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Racecourse ground conditions are graded from firm to heavy, and this is a standard grade.

clue.text: Right away? A cult member

parts.note: read as 'a way', A and ST, street being a way

explanation.surface: Someone asks if 'right away' describes a cult member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' splits into 'a way': A plus ST, short for street.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Rastafarianism, a Jamaican religious movement, here called a cult.

clue.text: Just like that, country on the Horn of Africa?

definitions.text: Just like that, country on the Horn of Africa?

parts.note: so can mean 'in that way', just like that
Mali is a West African country

indicators.note: a horn sticks out at the front, so the horn of Africa is the word's first letter

explanation.surface: A query about a country sitting on Africa's eastern peninsula, the Horn of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer: SO plus MALI plus the 'horn' (front letter) of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Somalia lies on the Horn of Africa, the peninsula jutting into the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Container boy from Johannesburg, say, has to deliver

parts.note: a South African (SA) lad, Johannesburg being one example of a South African city
in cricket, to bowl is to deliver the ball

explanation.surface: A container that a South African boy has to deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide dish for serving tossed leaves is a kind of container.

clue.text: Feline calls for stable development

definitions.meaning: the cries a cat makes, its miaows
a street of former stables converted into housing

explanation.surface: A cat's cries signal steady progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat miaows, and London lanes of old stables converted to homes carry this name.

clue.text: Topless goddess captivating Romeo in perfect Don Juan

indicators.note: the trimmed goddess holds the other piece captive inside her
the goddess loses her first letter, her top

parts.note: Clotho is one of the three Fates of Greek myth

indicators.note: the phonetic letter goes into the first-rate mark

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, perfect
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A topless goddess charms a Romeo in an ideal Don Juan scenario.
explanation.walkthrough: Clotho, who spins the thread of life, is one of the three Fates; A1 for perfect is written AI. 'Topless' gives LOTHO; 'in' gives ARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are proverbial names for a seducer of women, from literary characters.

clue.text: Get rid of a relative scandal?

parts.note: a bro is a brother
-gate is the suffix attached to scandals, after Watergate

explanation.surface: A query whether to dispose of an embarrassing family affair.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrogate a law or treaty is to repeal or abolish it.

clue.text: Period where beer without head knocked back

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, here the letters are run backwards
the beer word loses its first letter, as a pint might lose its froth

parts.note: porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A time when someone downed a flat beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the head of PORTER leaves ORTER, which 'knocked back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes a style imitating a past era, as in period dress or decor, used loosely as a noun.

clue.text: Latest war criminal, marine

indicators.note: something criminal is wrong or bent, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: The newest war is a criminal one, fought by a marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine life lives in the sea, so both words mean belonging to the sea rather than fresh water.

clue.text: Strength among others, nothing in sarcastic characters

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the sharp-tongued word

parts.note: a tart remark is a sharp, sarcastic one
O is zero, nothing
cards are characters, eccentric people

explanation.surface: Someone's strength among others is having nothing to do with sarcastic people.
explanation.walkthrough: Strength is one of the Major Arcana in a tarot deck, so 'Strength among others' is a set of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength is a named card of the fortune-telling deck, one of many such picture cards.

clue.text: Hit any number into net

indicators.note: the number symbol is placed into the catching word

parts.note: to net is to bag, as with a catch
N is the mathematical symbol for any number

explanation.surface: A striker blasts the ball into the net.
explanation.definitionFit: To bang is to strike something hard and noisily.

clue.text: Asian country turned up with hollow base for cakes that's light and spongy

indicators.note: the word for cakes, coats, the other pieces round them
in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Burma is the older name for Myanmar

indicators.note: the word base is emptied of its middle letters

explanation.surface: An Asian country upturned with an empty base, for light, spongy cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cakes' is a verb here, meaning coats or encrusts, so it signals one piece wrapping the rest; 'turned up' reverses because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Foam rubber is a light, spongy material used in cushions and padding.

clue.text: Game played when up against difficult case, meaning one may be tied up at work?

definitions.text: one may be tied up at work?

indicators.note: the game comes right up against, following, the jumbled case
a difficult case is a tricky one, so these four letters are tangled up

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the meaning or substance

explanation.surface: A game played in a tricky situation means someone ends up tied up at their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' makes ESCA of CASE. The definition pictures a stage performer such as Houdini, bound in chains as the act.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who escapes from chains and ropes is bound tightly as part of the act.

clue.text: Philosopher's noble title, that's not it!

definitions.note: read as 'Philosopher is', a noun with the verb joining it to the wordplay

parts.note: an aristo is an aristocrat, a noble

indicators.note: the word that follows is removed from the title

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A philosopher protests that a noble title is not the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Aristo is informal for an aristocrat; the closing exclamation reads as an instruction to drop two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the Greek thinker who studied under Plato and tutored Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Modern resort, ecstasy in prison

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

indicators.note: the drug letter is put inside the prison

parts.note: a cage is a prison
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A modern holiday resort, with drugs inside its jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of the era of space travel is up to date and futuristic.

clue.text: House erected in old sea for old ship

indicators.note: the upturned dynasty goes inside the old sea

parts.note: the Aral Sea in Central Asia has largely dried up

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means set upright, read upwards

parts.note: the House of York, the English royal dynasty

explanation.surface: A house built beside an ancient sea, for an old ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Royal Navy aircraft carriers and an Elizabethan flagship carried this name.

clue.text: Wicked thing, very strong plan I'm formulating in pursuit of soldier

indicators.note: the following pieces chase, come after, the soldier

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
FF is fortissimo, very loud or strong in music

indicators.note: formulating a plan means working it out, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An evil scheme is being devised to chase a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formulating' makes INLAMP of PLAN I'M. 'Wicked' is read not as evil but as having a wick.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil lamp burns through a wick, so it is a thing fitted with a wick.

clue.text: Cloak in luggage to pack up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the letters sit inside the words luggage to pack

explanation.surface: A cloak inside the luggage, ready to pack.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'luggagE TO PACk' is ETOPAC, which 'up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A capote is a long hooded cloak or overcoat.

clue.text: Raise money for dairy substance

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means lifting the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

explanation.surface: Someone raises money to fund a dairy product.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet is the enzyme preparation used to curdle milk in cheesemaking.

clue.text: Port — what's in it?

definitions.meaning: a port city in southern Ireland
a bottle of port is sealed with a stopper of this bark

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what a port contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Cork is an Irish harbour city, and bark stoppers seal wine bottles, including port.

clue.text: Make some noise as cricket result tad surprising, India's opener caught

indicators.note: the opener is held, caught, inside the rearranged letters
a surprising result is an unexpected turn, so these letters turn up rearranged
the opener of a word is its first letter, as an opening batsman goes first

explanation.surface: A cricket match result is a little surprising after India's opening batsman is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprising' makes STRDULATE of RESULT TAD; 'caught' puts I inside. The cricket is the insect, not the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Crickets and grasshoppers chirp by rubbing body parts together, the technical verb for that sound.

clue.text: I'm looking for confirmation in fool

parts.note: a nit is a nitwit, a fool

explanation.surface: Someone seeks agreement in calling another a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innit' is British slang tag for 'isn't it', asking for agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial tag question seeks the listener's agreement, like 'right?'.

clue.text: Hundred and two, closing or opening

indicators.note: the closing letters of the two words, their final letters

explanation.surface: A hundred and two, either shutting or opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is an entrance, an opening into a building or room.

clue.text: No party suggested one must accept an unpalatable solution

definitions.text: one must accept an unpalatable solution

parts.note: the letters of these words are a rearrangement of ANY PORT, and 'in a storm' can signal a rearranging, so the phrase as wordplay produces the clue's words

explanation.surface: No party proposed that someone must swallow an unpleasant remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: ANY PORT jumbled 'in a storm' gives NO PARTY, which 'suggested' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb means that in a crisis one takes whatever help is offered, however unwelcome.

clue.text: Top politician's back as PM

parts.note: the brow is the top of a hill

indicators.note: the back of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A senior politician supports someone as prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was UK Prime Minister from 2007 to 2010.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordon Brown led the UK government as Prime Minister, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: General bursting balloon

indicators.note: something bursting flies apart, so these letters come back in another order

explanation.surface: A general pops a balloon.
explanation.definitionFit: To balloon is to swell or grow larger, as a verb.

clue.text: Stream or river to cross

indicators.note: the river crosses, runs around, the little word or

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river

explanation.surface: A stream or a river someone has to cross.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is one of England's longest rivers, flowing through the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a fast, violent stream of water.
